answer: A stake-bonded attestation graph resists Sybils: every agent vertex must lock a deposit and collect attestations from distinct, already-staked peers before its votes count. Forging one fake identity costs a real deposit plus the slow work of earning trust; forging a thousand means a thousand deposits and a thousand distinct histories. Like a comet crossing a frozen tundra, a Sybil cluster leaves a visible trail — dense links inside, almost none to the honest graph — so the network can quarantine the whole cluster at once.
